html: The Tsankupi were a band of the Kalapuya people of Oregon's Willamette Valley, living along the Calapooia River near present Brownsville. The Kalapuya burned the valley's grasslands every year to keep open oak savanna, where they gathered camas bulbs, acorns and tarweed seeds and hunted deer. A malaria epidemic in the early 1830s killed most of the valley's people, and settlers on the Oregon Trail took the land that remained. In 1855 the Kalapuya bands signed the Willamette Valley Treaty and were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation. Other bands included the Santiam.
